decisions.title: Regional stamps: one region, or two or more regions behind Front Door
decisions.costNote: The figures are the private endpoints of one stamp. Each additional stamp repeats every regional cost (API Management, the Functions apps, private endpoints, and the registry's read or write regions), which the later decisions show per region.

impact.covers: Zone failures, if the stamp's components are zone-redundant.
impact.uncovered: A region failure denies every developer.
impact.sla: Per component; see the other decisions.

options.label: Two or more stamps serving at once, behind Front Door

impact.covers: Zone and region failures; Front Door removes an unhealthy origin from rotation.
impact.uncovered: A failure of a shared global dependency (Microsoft Entra ID, Front Door, the backend) still denies the developers it serves.

options.notDeployableByCore: D1 to D3 deploy one region today (WP-CORE availability schema: region.mode single-region)

options.label: A primary stamp and a standby stamp, behind Front Door priority routing

impact.covers: Region failures, after Front Door's health probes fail the primary over.
impact.uncovered: Developers are denied during failover; the standby's capacity must match the primary's.

options.notDeployableByCore: D1 to D3 deploy one region today (WP-CORE availability schema: region.mode single-region)

recommendation.reason: ADR-0014 decision 2 requires at least two regional stamps for production. API Management v2 has no multi-region deployment, so regions are separate stamps behind Front Door; Azure Functions recommends an active-active pattern with Front Door.

decisions.title: Stamp regions, primary first, chosen from the candidate regions

recommendation.rule: Regions where every chosen option passes its constraints; for two stamps, prefer a pair inside one data-residency geography (for India: centralindia with southindia, of which only centralindia has availability zones).
recommendation.reason: Residency stays inside the geography and a region failure leaves a stamp.

decisions.title: API Management tier and zone redundancy for each stamp

impact.covers: A single compute failure: each unit has two compute resources.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure denies every developer of the stamp. Zone redundancy cannot be added after creation.
impact.sla: 99.95% (SLA, single region; pricing page lists 99.95% for Standard v2).

impact.covers: A zone failure: units are spread across zones best-effort.
impact.uncovered: A region failure denies every developer of the stamp. Up to 10 units per instance; 25,000 subscriptions per instance (ADR-0006).
impact.sla: 99.95% (SLA document and pricing page; no zone figure is stated for Standard v2).

impact.covers: A single compute failure; dedicated compute; virtual network injection.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure denies every developer of the stamp. Zone redundancy cannot be added after creation.

impact.covers: A zone failure; up to 30 units per instance; virtual network injection; 75,000 subscriptions per instance (ADR-0006).
impact.uncovered: A region failure denies every developer of the stamp.
impact.sla: 99.99% on the pricing page with units in two or more zones; the SLA document states 99.95% for one region and 99.99% for Premium across two or more regions, and does not name the v2 tiers (U-new-HADEC-1).

recommendation.reason: It survives a zone failure, scales to 30 units per instance against 10, includes requests without a per-call meter, and supports full network isolation. Zone redundancy is set only at creation.

decisions.title: API Management units per stamp

recommendation.reason: Units = ceil(peak requests per second / measured requests per second per unit). With zone redundancy over Z zones, ceil(units x Z / (Z - 1)), at least 2, keeps the peak served after one zone is lost if units are spread evenly; the spread is best-effort. Microsoft states throughput figures must not be used for capacity planning and a load test must measure them (P-12).

decisions.title: Azure Front Door in front of the stamps

impact.covers: Nothing global.
impact.uncovered: With one stamp, a region failure denies everyone; with several stamps there is no health-based routing between them.

options.label: Front Door Standard

impact.covers: Region failure, by health probes and priority or weighted routing across stamps.
impact.uncovered: No Private Link to origins and no managed WAF rules: origins stay publicly reachable.

options.notDeployableByCore: D1 does not create Front Door today

options.label: Front Door Premium

impact.covers: Region failure, as Standard; Private Link to origins and managed WAF rules and bot protection.
impact.uncovered: A Front Door failure denies everyone routed through it.

options.notDeployableByCore: D1 does not create Front Door today

recommendation.reason: Two or more stamps need global health-based routing. Premium adds Private Link to origins, so the gateways need not be public, and managed WAF rules.

decisions.title: Registry (Cosmos DB) capacity mode and zone redundancy

impact.covers: Nothing beyond the platform's single-zone redundancy.
impact.uncovered: A zone or region failure denies everyone once cached decisions expire. Serverless runs in one region only; conversion to provisioned is irreversible.
impact.sla: The SLA document gives figures for provisioned throughput only.

options.label: Serverless, one region, zone-redundant (only at account creation)

impact.covers: A zone failure.
impact.uncovered: A region failure denies everyone once cached decisions expire.
impact.sla: The SLA document gives figures for provisioned throughput only.

options.label: Provisioned throughput, manual RU/s, no zones

impact.covers: Requests up to the provisioned RU/s; more regions can be added.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure denies everyone in a one-region account once cached decisions expire. Above the RU/s, requests are rate-limited (429).
impact.sla: 99.99% one region; 99.999% reads with two or more regions (SLA).

impact.covers: A zone failure.
impact.uncovered: A region failure, unless more regions are added. Above the RU/s, requests are rate-limited (429).

impact.covers: Load between 10% of the maximum and the maximum RU/s without a change.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure denies everyone in a one-region account once cached decisions expire.

impact.covers: A zone failure and load changes up to the maximum RU/s.
impact.uncovered: A region failure, unless more regions are added.
impact.sla: 99.995% one region with zones; 99.999% reads with two or more regions (SLA).

recommendation.reason: Zones are included at no premium for autoscale, multi-region reads are possible, and serverless is limited to one region with irreversible conversion. Zone redundancy is set when a region is added.

decisions.title: Registry RU/s (manual) or maximum RU/s (autoscale); not asked for serverless

recommendation.reason: RU/s = peak reads per second x RU per read + peak writes per second x RU per write, rounded up to a multiple of 100 (manual, at least 400) or of 1,000 (autoscale: the entry point is 1,000 RU/s and the maximum is set in increments of 1,000).

decisions.title: Registry regions

impact.covers: As the capacity decision.
impact.uncovered: A region failure denies everyone once cached decisions expire.

options.label: A read region in each stamp region, one write region

impact.covers: A region failure for reads; each stamp reads locally.
impact.uncovered: Writes (sync, onboarding) stop until failover; service-managed failover can take an hour or more.

impact.covers: A region failure for reads and writes.
impact.uncovered: Conflicting writes in two regions resolve by the account's conflict policy.

recommendation.reason: The request path only reads the registry; one write region keeps sync and onboarding simple, and a region failure leaves every stamp reading.

decisions.title: Resolver instance memory

impact.covers: Lowest memory cost per instance.
impact.uncovered: Fewer concurrent requests per instance; more scale-out.

impact.covers: The size the PoC resolver runs today.
impact.uncovered: As the other sizes.

impact.covers: Most concurrency per instance.
impact.uncovered: Highest memory cost per instance.

recommendation.reason: The PoC resolver runs at 2,048 MB (WP-RES, read 2026-10-11); P-12 measures whether another size serves the peak at lower cost.

decisions.title: Resolver Function App (Flex Consumption) zone redundancy

impact.covers: A zone failure: always-ready instances are spread across at least two zones.
impact.uncovered: A region failure denies everyone of the stamp once cached decisions expire. At least two always-ready instances per function group, billed while idle.

impact.covers: Instance failures, replaced by the platform.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure can deny everyone of the stamp once cached decisions expire.

recommendation.reason: The resolver is on the request path for cache misses; zone redundancy has no separate meter, only the two always-ready instances it requires.

decisions.title: Resolver always-ready instances

recommendation.reason: Two: zone redundancy requires at least two always-ready instances per function group, and warm instances remove cold starts from the request path.

decisions.title: Resolver maximum on-demand instances

recommendation.reason: At least the peak concurrent resolver calls divided by one instance's concurrency, which P-12 measures. The PoC runs 40 (WP-RES).

decisions.title: Cache for fail-static resolutions

impact.covers: Resolver latency during normal operation.
impact.uncovered: The built-in cache is shared per region and is not guaranteed to persist; entries lost during a resolver or registry outage cannot be served last-known-good.

options.label: Azure Managed Redis, Balanced tier, high availability

impact.covers: Resolver and registry outages within the stale-serve limit; a zone failure when the region has zones (automatic for high availability).
impact.uncovered: A region failure, unless each stamp has its own cache. Without high availability there is no SLA.

options.notDeployableByCore: D1 does not create Azure Managed Redis today

options.label: Azure Managed Redis, Memory Optimized tier, high availability

impact.covers: As Balanced, with more memory per vCPU.
impact.uncovered: As Balanced.

options.notDeployableByCore: D1 does not create Azure Managed Redis today

options.label: Azure Managed Redis, Compute Optimized tier, high availability

impact.covers: As Balanced, with most throughput per GB.
impact.uncovered: As Balanced.

options.notDeployableByCore: D1 does not create Azure Managed Redis today

recommendation.reason: Fail-static serving needs entries that survive gateway updates and zone failures; the built-in cache is volatile. Balanced suits a small key-value working set; P-12 confirms the size.

decisions.title: Azure Managed Redis SKU (validated against the live price list for the chosen tier)

recommendation.rule: The smallest SKU whose memory holds the cached resolutions with headroom; B0 and B1 do not support active geo-replication.
recommendation.reason: Cost scales with SKU size.

decisions.title: Cache replication across stamps

impact.covers: Each stamp's own outage of the resolver or registry.
impact.uncovered: A developer routed to another stamp after a region failure starts with an empty cache there.

options.label: Active geo-replication across the stamps (up to five instances)

impact.covers: Last-known-good entries are present in every stamp after a region failure.
impact.uncovered: Replication is eventually consistent, with no SLA on sync time.
impact.sla: 99.999% with three or more regions, each highly available and zone-redundant (SLA).

recommendation.reason: After a region failure, the surviving stamp can still serve last-known-good decisions for developers it has not served before.

decisions.title: Storage account redundancy for the Function Apps

impact.covers: A zone failure of the apps' deployment and host storage.
impact.uncovered: A region failure.

impact.covers: Disk and rack failures inside one datacenter.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure can stop the apps that depend on the storage.

recommendation.reason: Zone-redundant apps should not depend on storage that a single zone failure stops.

decisions.title: Group sync app placement across stamp regions

options.label: One app, in the primary stamp region

impact.covers: As its zone decision.
impact.uncovered: A region failure delays membership changes until the region recovers; records persist, so nobody loses access.

options.label: An app in every stamp region; a lease lets one instance write

impact.covers: A region failure: another region's app takes the lease.
impact.uncovered: A failure of the shared registry or of Microsoft Graph.

recommendation.reason: The sync is off the request path and its records persist: a region outage delays changes and denies no one.

decisions.title: Group sync instance memory

impact.covers: Lowest memory cost per instance.
impact.uncovered: Longer runs for large reads.

impact.covers: The common size.
impact.uncovered: As the other sizes.

impact.covers: Most memory per instance.
impact.uncovered: Highest memory cost per instance.

decisions.title: Group sync Function App zone redundancy

impact.covers: Instance failures.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure delays additions and removals until the app recovers; records persist, so nobody loses access (ADR-0008).

impact.covers: A zone failure.
impact.uncovered: A region failure delays changes.

recommendation.reason: The sync is off the request path and its records persist: an outage delays membership changes and denies no one, so two billed always-ready instances buy little.

decisions.title: Group sync always-ready instances (at least 2 when zone-redundant)

recommendation.reason: None for a timer-triggered sync without zone redundancy; zone redundancy requires at least two.

decisions.title: Group sync maximum on-demand instances

recommendation.reason: One run at a time holds the lease, so a small number suffices; the lease prevents overlapping writers.

options.label: One app, in the primary stamp region

impact.covers: As its zone decision.
impact.uncovered: A region failure stops budget updates; beyond the budget-state hard limit every person is refused.

options.label: An app in every stamp region; a lease lets one instance write

impact.covers: A region failure: another region's app takes the lease.
impact.uncovered: A failure of the shared registry or of Microsoft Graph.

recommendation.reason: A reconciler outage longer than the hard limit denies everyone; docs/AVAILABILITY.md section 3 row 6 runs it in two regions with a lease.

decisions.title: Reconciler instance memory

impact.covers: Lowest memory cost per instance.
impact.uncovered: Longer runs for large reads.

impact.covers: The common size.
impact.uncovered: As the other sizes.

impact.covers: Most memory per instance.
impact.uncovered: Highest memory cost per instance.

decisions.title: Reconciler Function App zone redundancy

impact.covers: A zone failure: budget state stays fresh.
impact.uncovered: A region failure: budget state goes stale and, beyond the hard limit, every person is refused (WP-RES).

impact.covers: Instance failures.
impact.uncovered: A zone failure stops budget updates; beyond the hard limit every person is refused.

recommendation.reason: A reconciler outage longer than the budget-state hard limit denies everyone, so it carries the same zone requirement as the request path.

decisions.title: Reconciler always-ready instances (at least 2 when zone-redundant)

recommendation.reason: Zone redundancy requires at least two; without it, none for a timer-triggered app.

decisions.title: Reconciler maximum on-demand instances

recommendation.reason: A lease lets one instance write (docs/AVAILABILITY.md section 3 row 6); more instances add no throughput.

decisions.title: Analytics retention in days

costBasis.label: 61 days, that is 30 days beyond the 31 included

recommendation.reason: 31 days are included in the ingestion price; a longer period follows the customer's audit and investigation needs.

decisions.title: Log Analytics workspace region

recommendation.rule: The primary stamp's region, if it offers Log Analytics.
recommendation.reason: Gateway logs stay in the data-residency geography and next to the gateway.

decisions.title: Log Analytics workspace replication

impact.covers: Zone failures handled by the service in the region.
impact.uncovered: A region failure stops alerts and the usage ledger; the reconciler then marks scopes 'telemetry missing' and budget state ages towards the hard limit.

options.label: Replicate to a secondary region in the same region group

impact.covers: A region failure, after a manual switchover; only logs ingested after enabling are replicated.
impact.uncovered: Data collection rules not associated with the workspace's endpoint are billed but not replicated; Auxiliary tables are not supported.

recommendation.reason: Usage records feed budgets and alerts; a region outage without a replica leaves both blind.

decisions.title: Workspace replication secondary region (any region of the same replication group)

recommendation.rule: A secondary region of the workspace region's replication group; for centralindia, southindia.
recommendation.reason: Replication is allowed only inside the documented region groups.

decisions.title: Seconds an allow decision is served before the resolver is asked again

recommendation.reason: A removal takes effect within the sync interval plus this value (docs/PILOT.md, enforcement table); shorter values send more resolver calls.

decisions.title: Seconds a refusal is cached

recommendation.reason: A newly added member waits up to the sync interval plus this value; short values protect the resolver less from repeated refused calls.

decisions.title: Maximum stale-serve time: seconds after the allow TTL that a last-known-good allow is served while the resolver fails

recommendation.reason: Long enough to ride out a resolver or registry outage, short enough that a removed person's access ends within the organisation's tolerance. 0 turns off last-known-good serving: during a resolver outage each request is refused once its cached allow expires (ADR-0014 decision 1; WP-GW schema).

decisions.title: Seconds a last-known-good allow is served after a failed refresh before the resolver is asked again (at most the maximum stale-serve time when that is above 0)

recommendation.reason: 30 to 120 seconds (WP-GW): during a resolver outage each expired allow asks the failing resolver at most once per backoff, and last-known-good is served meanwhile; shorter values load the resolver more, longer values delay recovery. The pilot runs 30 (coordinator pilot decision).

decisions.title: Retry-After seconds sent with a 503 when no last-known-good allow exists

recommendation.reason: Long enough not to amplify an outage with client retries.

decisions.title: Budget-state grace window (seconds after validUntil served with the last ceiling, flagged degraded)

recommendation.reason: At least two reconciler intervals, so one missed run degrades nobody's access; the PoC runs 600 (WP-RES).

decisions.title: Budget-state hard limit (seconds after validUntil after which requests are refused)

recommendation.reason: Not below the grace window; it bounds overspend during a reconciler or telemetry outage, and beyond it every person is refused (WP-RES AC5). The PoC runs 3,600.

decisions.title: Sync interval in minutes (exported as the NCRONTAB schedule 0 */N * * * *)

recommendation.reason: 5 to 15 minutes at 500,000 people: each run reads every entitlement document; removals take up to one interval plus the gateway cache TTL (WP-SYNC).

decisions.title: Removals always allowed in one sync run

recommendation.reason: About the largest routine offboarding batch per interval (WP-SYNC).

decisions.title: Fraction of memberships one run may remove beyond the count

recommendation.reason: 0.01 to 0.05 at 500,000 people; with the count it bounds a mass revocation (WP-SYNC).

decisions.title: Sync lease seconds (WP-CORE's schema allows 1 to 3,600; WP-SYNC accepts up to 86,400)

recommendation.reason: 300 to 900: above clock skew and the longest Graph wait (WP-SYNC).

decisions.title: Gateway timeout for one resolver call

recommendation.reason: Above the resolver's p99 latency measured by P-12 and below the client's patience; a timeout falls back to last-known-good.
recommendation.rule: Above the resolver's p99 latency measured by P-12 and below the client's patience; a timeout falls back to last-known-good.

decisions.title: Per-person admission: calls per renewal period, before any resolver call

recommendation.reason: Above the heaviest legitimate Claude Code use; it stops one runaway client from consuming resolver capacity for others.
recommendation.rule: Above the heaviest legitimate Claude Code use; it stops one runaway client from consuming resolver capacity for others.

decisions.title: Per-person admission renewal period in seconds (rate-limit-by-key allows at most 300)

recommendation.reason: Matches the calls value above.

decisions.title: Resolver-miss admission: calls per renewal period (applies to cache misses only; a refresh of an expired allow is not refused by it)

recommendation.reason: At most what the resolver serves, measured by P-12; the reference's ADR-0017 admitted 200 per second.
recommendation.rule: At most what the resolver serves, measured by P-12; the reference's ADR-0017 admitted 200 per second.

decisions.title: Resolver-miss admission renewal period in seconds

recommendation.reason: Matches the calls value above.

decisions.title: Concurrent resolver calls per gateway

recommendation.reason: At most the resolver's measured concurrency; the reference's ADR-0017 admitted 100.
recommendation.rule: At most the resolver's measured concurrency; the reference's ADR-0017 admitted 100.

decisions.title: WP-TEL alert configuration id holding the recipients and thresholds the operations team approved

recommendation.rule: The approved configuration; recipients an on-call group mailbox, not a person; thresholds per docs/TELEMETRY.md.
recommendation.reason: Recipients are personal data and stay in WP-TEL's configuration; this record binds the decision to it by id and digest.

decisions.decidedIn: D2 answers: telemetry.alertConfigurationFile (WP-CORE); recipients and thresholds in WP-TEL's alert configuration

decisions.title: SHA-256 of that alert configuration file (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256, lower case)

recommendation.rule: The digest of the approved file.
recommendation.reason: A later edit of the file no longer matches the recorded decision.

decisions.title: Backend failover members, order and data-zone limit, per designated subscription

recommendation.rule: Two or more Claude deployments in different regions of the designated subscription, inside the data zone the project allows, behind an APIM backend pool with circuit breakers.
recommendation.reason: A Global Standard or Data Zone Standard deployment does not move a region's traffic elsewhere: 'if the primary region experiences an interruption in service, all traffic initially routed to this region is affected'. No data zone covers India.

decisions.title: Backend authentication mode

recommendation.rule: Managed identity in the gateway's tenant (shape A); across tenants, a federated credential where the other tenant allows it, otherwise a certificate broker; a client secret only with automated rotation and an expiry alert.
recommendation.reason: An expired secret denies everyone on that backend (docs/AVAILABILITY.md section 3 row 9).

cosmos-serverless-zr.label: Request units consumed (the zone multiplier for serverless is not published: U-new-HADEC-3)

cosmos-autoscale.label: Autoscale maximum RU/s x 1.5, every hour at the maximum (upper bound; the floor is 10% of it)

cosmos-multi-write.label: Multi-region write RU/s in this region (no autoscale or zone premium)

flex-resolver.label: Execution time at the on-demand rate, with instances fully packed at the measured concurrency (an estimate, not a bound: U-new-HADEC-5)
